body.statement: Determine the finite value of \(r_\beta(\ell)\) exactly for every \(\ell\ge4\).  Using \(\mathfrak H_{\ell}\), classify each unresolved intermediate order \(L_\ell\le R<U_\ell\).  At every order where \(\beta\) is generically constant on legal fibers, give a terminating algebraic recovery atlas whose domains cover a nonempty relatively Zariski-open subset of \(\mathcal O_{\ell,R}\), whose covering charts return the common effect, and whose uncovered legal inputs return \(\bot\).  At every smaller unresolved order, construct a Zariski-dense relatively Euclidean-open subset of the legal image whose fibers contain independent finite-support unequal-\(\beta\) twins.  The first remaining elbow is \((\ell,R)=(4,3)\): decide its complete saturated target projection and certify every surviving real branch against the finite-atomic moment constraints.  The established exact values are \(r_\beta(1)=r_\beta(2)=3\) and \(r_\beta(3)=4\), so none of these cases remains part of the question.
body.justification: The residual kernel is the exact classification of every still-unresolved intermediate-order legal fiber for \(\ell\ge4\).
body.gap: The closest paper gives only \(k(\ell)\)-order sufficiency, and the present upper and lower constructions do not meet at every finite \(\ell\ge4\).
body.consumer: Completing the residual question would fix the remaining minimum moment orders and choose between a point recovery map and confidence-fiber output at each intermediate depth.

obligation.what_is_open: Determine \(r_\beta(\ell)\) for every remaining \(\ell\ge4\), beginning with the complete legal target projection at \((\ell,R)=(4,3)\).
obligation.obstruction: The two-latent finite branch is now eliminated exactly, but neither the contraction upper bound nor the weight-saturation lower construction classifies the intermediate orders \(L_\ell\le R<U_\ell\) for all \(\ell\ge4\). Those fibers can mix positive-dimensional loading variation with discrete decomposition branches, and their target projection and real moment feasibility have not yet been certified.
obligation.attempted: The prescribed first elbow \((2,3)\) was reduced to an observable covariance--third-cumulant identity. Its linear factorization proved that the unequal-effect saturation is empty on a nonempty legal chart, so the proposed open-twin architecture was correctly abandoned there. No claim about the still different \((4,3)\) incidence geometry is inferred from that calculation.
obligation.partial_result:
The complete \((\ell,R)=(2,3)\) target projection is now closed.  On the observable chart \(\Delta_{2,3}=\det(M_3)a_1\ne0\), the polynomial \(\mathcal P_\zeta(q)\) factors as
\[
 \mathcal P_\zeta(q)=\det(M_3)(\beta-q)
 \left\{\kappa^S_{t,2}-\kappa^S_{t,3}\lambda_2^{\mathsf T}
 \Lambda_3^{-1}V^{-1}(0,1,0)^{\mathsf T}\right\}.
\]
Thus its target rational-univariate representation is linear, every legal representation has \(\beta=-a_0/a_1\), and the unequal-effect incidence localization is empty.  The explicit legal point in the proof has \(\mathcal P_\zeta(q)=50(2-q)\) and \(\Delta_{2,3}=-300\).  Consequently
\[
 r_\beta(1)=3,\qquad r_\beta(2)=3,\qquad r_\beta(3)=4,
\]
while the established global bounds remain
\[
 L_\ell\le r_\beta(\ell)\le U_\ell,
 \qquad \frac{r_\beta(\ell)}{\sqrt{2\ell}}\longrightarrow1.
\]
The unresolved finite cases begin at \((\ell,R)=(4,3)\).
